text: and so you see now in that case, you have something like 4 angles to chase before even considering it might be one layer up from all of this
resolution: Closing synthesis of the whack-a-mole thread (req_3469, 3474-3482; oracle consulted throughout the thread, no new approach decided this turn): confirmed the user's point that every incident presents ~4 plausible lower layers to chase — the op's own algorithm, the mirror/sync relay, a silent refusal gate, and runtime staleness (pre-fix binary / hot-reload not covering Zig), plus the GPU cache family — and each of the 52 hunts found a REAL culprit in one of them, which is precisely what shielded the architecture layer from suspicion: every search ends at a satisfying local conviction, so nobody continues upward. Also noted the user is structurally the only continuous observer across incidents (sessions are ephemeral), which is why the meta-pattern was theirs to spot; the cross-incident diagnosis is now durably recorded in project memory (project_mesh_consistency_matrix) so future sessions inherit it instead of re-deriving from one incident. No code changed — discussion capstone.
